study type: secondary analysis of a prospective cohort
exposure: maternal indications (primarily preeclampsia) for medically indicated delivery
fetal indications (nonreassuring antenatal testing or worsening effusions) for medically indicated delivery
outcome: frequency of preterm birth (<37 weeks' gestation)
reasons for preterm birth (spontaneous vs. medically indicated)
frequency of neonatal death following preterm birth
cohort: The study included 56 pregnancies complicated by nonimmune hydrops fetalis (NIHF) that underwent exome sequencing if standard testing was nondiagnostic.
finding: More than four-fifths (86%) of pregnancies complicated by nonimmune hydrops fetalis (NIHF) result in preterm birth, often due to medically indicated delivery for nonreassuring fetal status, with neither fetal genetic diagnosis nor polyhydramnios being associated with preterm birth.
gest_age: Median gestational age at delivery was 32.8 weeks (interquartile range: 30.3-35.0), with preterm birth defined as <37 weeks' gestation.
